review_notes: Independently read all 1128 owned lines in canonical and rendered form, all subject and link pages, the entire 1453-line proposal, functionality.md, the entire coverage.json disposition ledger, link-dispositions.json, compiled-evidence.json and unresolved.json. No replacement proposal or mutations are submitted.
All 43 proposed writes target owned subjects. Links, entities, merges and follow_ups are empty. Semantic names remain hypotheses rather than canonical renames.

The proposal correctly distinguishes the state buffer from the SIS command stream, documents reverse scanning from x6C, exact-fill and u16-wrap hazards, and distinguishes high-bit-controlled deletion from low-bit-controlled restoration.

Measurement corrections are supported: termination at opcodes 1,2,3,7; conditional continuation at 0; raw final spacing subtraction; restoration of x78.x but not x78.y; and persistence of allocation or lower-stack mutations. CalcTextSize is retained only as an approximate semantic name, not a promise of whole-stream or exact final-geometry measurement.

The renderer's opcode6 attribution is correct in the current proposal: stream operands replace delay locals initially seeded from x90/x92. Glyphs and opcode26 use the first local; newline uses the second.

Foreign definitions and consumers confirm the apparent SIS field-name inversion: textures supplies metric bytes and kerning supplies image bytes. HSD_SisLib_BytePtr is a plain void*-to-u8* conversion, not a resource transformation.
Foreign hsd_3A64 conversion compares external pairs and emits corresponding internal pairs. Its ARRAY_SIZE bound is 287 from sislib_font.h, whereas each owned array has 288 pairs.

Compiled evidence inventories both existing objects, their section hashes, symbols and all dispatch-table relocations. It supports the explicitly scoped existing-object .data layout claims. This is not a claim that a new build was performed or that all machine code matches.

Archive delegate definitions, parsing and external-chain processing were checked independently. Sislib consumers load named resources and tear down text users before archive release. The corrected destructor wording does not mistake two assertions for provenance validation.

Optional paths and exceptional arithmetic are specifically deferred below where the proposal makes no stronger claim. Acceptance is semantic approval of the submitted changes, not runtime safety certification.

unresolved.detail: render_callback executes synchronously only in GObj mode after resource pointers and sis_cursor have been captured. The renderer continues using text and those pointers without lifetime validation. Safety if the callback destroys the text, replaces stream storage, unloads resources or recursively renders is not established and is not implied by retained rendering claims.

No finite-value or positive-dimension checks exist. Equality at box width does not compress; NaN comparisons do not enter the ordinary overwidth branch. Division by measured width or glyph dimensions can produce exceptional results, and float-to-integer serialization is unchecked. Exact target behavior for NaN, infinities and out-of-range conversions remains unproved. No retained claim guarantees finite dimensions or safe clipping.

unresolved.topic: Shared SIS types and resource bounds
unresolved.detail: Observed field roles contradict apparent names. Correct replacement family types, custom resource extents and validity for every glyph code remain unresolved. font_idx is unchecked against the five-entry resource array. Masks used for glyph offsets are not bounds checks. Direct rendering leaves custom-resource locals null.

Existing-object inventory supports the submitted section layout statements. It does not establish a fresh build, whole-function machine-code equivalence, runtime object layouts of shared structs, or correctness of MUST_MATCH stack-relative matrix expressions. Those broader claims remain unresolved.

Exact-fill reverse reads, malformed payload starts, operand truncation, pointer cycles and alignment assumptions have no local safeguards. SisLib allocation is an arena allocator that rounds to four bytes and may panic; actual allocation extent can exceed recorded capacity. The proposal's 'can read past allocation' is a possibility, not a universal outcome for every exact-fill arena block.

Successful resource-lifecycle descriptions assume valid DAT contents. Parsing checks file-size equality but does not establish all section and relocation bounds; zero data_size can leave data null while flags satisfy destructor assertions. External-chain processing is bounded by data_size and terminator but general malformed-chain correctness is not proved.

Exact historical function names remain unknown. Generated glyph artwork was not independently reviewed, and no character-artwork or gameplay mapping is inferred from numeric glyph values. No facts existed for .sdata2 or the thirteen owned parameter subjects, and no new writes for those subjects are submitted.
